title: KCET 2016 Maths
subject: maths
source: KEA question paper (copy) + KEA answer key column A1

questions.q: The Set A has 4 elements and the Set B has 5 elements then the number of injective mappings that can be defined from A to B is
questions.explanation: Number of injective mappings from a 4-element set to a 5-element set is $^5P_4 = 5\times4\times3\times2 = 120$.

questions.q: Let f : R \to R be defined by f(x) = 2x + 6 which is a bijective mapping then $f^{-1}(x)$ is given by
questions.explanation: Put $y=2x+6$, solve for $x$: $x=\dfrac{y-6}{2}=\dfrac{y}{2}-3$, so $f^{-1}(x)=\dfrac{x}{2}-3$.

questions.q: Let $*$ be a binary operation defined on R by $a * b = \dfrac{a+b}{4}\ \forall\ a, b \in R$ then the operation $*$ is
questions.explanation: Since $a+b=b+a$, the operation is commutative; but $(a*b)*c=\dfrac{a+b+4c}{16}\ne a*(b*c)=\dfrac{4a+b+c}{16}$ in general, so it is not associative.

questions.q: The value of $\sin^{-1}\left(\cos\dfrac{53\pi}{5}\right)$ is
questions.explanation: $\dfrac{53\pi}{5}=10\pi+\dfrac{3\pi}{5}$, so $\cos\dfrac{53\pi}{5}=\cos\dfrac{3\pi}{5}=-\sin\dfrac{\pi}{10}$, giving $\sin^{-1}\left(-\sin\dfrac{\pi}{10}\right)=-\dfrac{\pi}{10}$.

questions.q: If $3\tan^{-1}x + \cot^{-1}x = \pi$ then x equal to
questions.explanation: Using $\cot^{-1}x=\dfrac{\pi}{2}-\tan^{-1}x$, we get $2\tan^{-1}x=\dfrac{\pi}{2}$, so $\tan^{-1}x=\dfrac{\pi}{4}$, giving $x=1$.

questions.q: The simplified form of $\tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{x}{y}\right) - \tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{x-y}{x+y}\right)$ is equal to
questions.explanation: This is a standard identity: $\tan^{-1}\dfrac{x}{y}-\tan^{-1}\dfrac{x-y}{x+y}=\dfrac{\pi}{4}$.

questions.q: If x y z are all different and not equal to zero and $\begin{vmatrix}1+x & 1 & 1\\ 1 & 1+y & 1\\ 1 & 1 & 1+z\end{vmatrix} = 0$ then the value of $x^{-1}+y^{-1}+z^{-1}$ is equal to
questions.explanation: Expanding the determinant gives $xyz+xy+yz+zx=0$; dividing by $xyz$ gives $1+x^{-1}+y^{-1}+z^{-1}=0$, so $x^{-1}+y^{-1}+z^{-1}=-1$.

questions.q: If A is any square matrix of order 3 \times 3 then $|3A|$ is equal to
questions.explanation: For an $n\times n$ matrix, $|kA|=k^n|A|$; here $n=3$, so $|3A|=3^3|A|=27|A|$.

questions.q: If $y = e^{\sin^{-1}(t^2-1)}$ & $x = e^{\sec^{-1}\left(\frac{1}{t^2-1}\right)}$ then $\dfrac{dy}{dx}$ is equal to
questions.explanation: With $u=t^2-1$, $\sec^{-1}(1/u)=\cos^{-1}u$, so $x=e^{\cos^{-1}u}$, $y=e^{\sin^{-1}u}$; differentiating gives $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=-\dfrac{y}{x}$.

questions.q: If $A=\dfrac{1}{\pi}\begin{bmatrix}\sin^{-1}(\pi x) & \tan^{-1}\left(\frac{x}{\pi}\right)\\ \sin^{-1}\left(\frac{x}{\pi}\right) & \cot^{-1}(\pi x)\end{bmatrix}$, $B=\dfrac{1}{\pi}\begin{bmatrix}-\cos^{-1}(\pi x) & \tan^{-1}\left(\frac{x}{\pi}\right)\\ \sin^{-1}\left(\frac{x}{\pi}\right) & -\tan^{-1}(\pi x)\end{bmatrix}$ then A - B is equal to
questions.explanation: Subtracting, the diagonal entries become $\dfrac{1}{\pi}[\sin^{-1}(\pi x)+\cos^{-1}(\pi x)]=\dfrac{1}{2}$ and $\dfrac{1}{\pi}[\cot^{-1}(\pi x)+\tan^{-1}(\pi x)]=\dfrac{1}{2}$, off-diagonal entries cancel, giving $A-B=\dfrac{1}{2}I$.

questions.q: If $x^y = e^{x-y}$ then $\dfrac{dy}{dx}$ is equal to
questions.explanation: Taking logs, $y\ln x = x-y \Rightarrow y=\dfrac{x}{1+\ln x}$; differentiating gives $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=\dfrac{\log x}{(1+\log x)^2}$.

questions.q: If A is a matrix of order m \times n and B is a matrix such that AB' and B'A are both defined, the order of the matrix B is
questions.explanation: For $AB'$ to be defined, $B'$ must have $n$ rows; for $B'A$ to be defined, $B'$ must have $m$ columns, so $B'$ is $n\times m$, hence $B$ is $m\times n$.

questions.q: The value of $\displaystyle\int \dfrac{e^x(1+x)\,dx}{\cos^2(e^x.x)}$ is equal to
questions.explanation: Substitute $u=xe^x$, so $du=e^x(1+x)\,dx$; the integral becomes $\int \sec^2u\,du=\tan u+c=\tan(xe^x)+c$.

questions.q: If x y z are not equal and \ne 0, \ne 1 the value of $\begin{vmatrix}\log x & \log y & \log z\\ \log 2x & \log 2y & \log 2z\\ \log 3x & \log 3y & \log 3z\end{vmatrix}$ is equal to
questions.explanation: Row 2 minus Row 1 gives the constant row $(\log 2,\log 2,\log 2)$ and Row 3 minus Row 1 gives $(\log 3,\log 3,\log 3)$; these two rows are proportional, so the determinant is 0.

questions.q: The function $f(x) = [x]$ where [x] the greatest integer function is continuous at
questions.explanation: The greatest integer function is discontinuous at every integer and continuous elsewhere; 1.5 is not an integer, so $f$ is continuous there.

questions.q: The value of $\displaystyle\int \dfrac{e^x(x^2\tan^{-1}x+\tan^{-1}x+1)}{x^2+1}\,dx$ is equal to
questions.explanation: The numerator equals $\tan^{-1}x(x^2+1)+1$, so the integrand simplifies to $e^x\left[\tan^{-1}x+\dfrac{1}{1+x^2}\right]$, which integrates (using $\int e^x[f+f']dx=e^xf$) to $e^x\tan^{-1}x+c$.

questions.q: If $2\vec{a}.\vec{b} = |\vec{a}|.|\vec{b}|$ then the angle between $\vec{a}$ & $\vec{b}$ is
questions.explanation: $2|\vec a||\vec b|\cos\theta=|\vec a||\vec b| \Rightarrow \cos\theta=\dfrac{1}{2} \Rightarrow \theta=60°$.

questions.q: If $x^m y^n = (x+y)^{m+n}$ then $\dfrac{dy}{dx}$ is equal to
questions.explanation: Taking logs and differentiating gives $\dfrac{m}{x}+\dfrac{n}{y}y'=\dfrac{m+n}{x+y}(1+y')$, which simplifies to $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=\dfrac{y}{x}$.

questions.q: The general solution of $\cot\theta + \tan\theta = 2$ is
questions.explanation: $\cot\theta+\tan\theta=\dfrac{2}{\sin2\theta}=2 \Rightarrow \sin2\theta=1 \Rightarrow 2\theta=n\pi+(-1)^n\dfrac{\pi}{2}$, so $\theta=\dfrac{n\pi}{2}+(-1)^n\dfrac{\pi}{4}$.

questions.q: The value of $\displaystyle\int_{-\pi/4}^{\pi/4}\sin^{103}x.\cos^{101}x\,dx$ is
questions.explanation: $\sin^{103}x\cos^{101}x$ is an odd function (odd power of sine times even power of cosine), so its integral over the symmetric interval $[-\pi/4,\pi/4]$ is 0.

questions.q: The length of latus rectum of the parabola $4y^2 + 3x + 3y + 1 = 0$ is
questions.explanation: Completing the square gives $\left(y+\dfrac{3}{8}\right)^2=-\dfrac{3}{4}\left(x+\dfrac{7}{48}\right)$, a parabola with $4a=\dfrac{3}{4}$, so the latus rectum is $3/4$.

questions.q: The value of $\displaystyle\int \dfrac{e^{6\log x}-e^{5\log x}}{e^{4\log x}-e^{3\log x}}\,dx$ is equal to
questions.explanation: Simplifying, $\dfrac{x^6-x^5}{x^4-x^3}=\dfrac{x^5(x-1)}{x^3(x-1)}=x^2$, and $\int x^2\,dx=\dfrac{x^3}{3}+c$.

questions.q: The differential coefficient of $\log_{10}x$ with respect to $\log_x 10$ is
questions.explanation: With $u=\log_{10}x$ and $v=\log_x10=1/u\cdot(\ln10/\ln10)$, differentiating $u$ and $v$ with respect to $x$ and dividing gives $\dfrac{du}{dv}=-(\log_{10}x)^2$.

questions.q: The slope of the tangent to the curve $x = t^2 + 3t - 8,\ y = 2t^2 - 2t - 5$ at the point (2, -1) is
questions.explanation: The point (2,-1) corresponds to $t=2$; then $dx/dt=2t+3=7$, $dy/dt=4t-2=6$, so slope $=dy/dx=6/7$.

questions.q: The real part of $(1 - \cos\theta + i\sin\theta)^{-1}$ is
questions.explanation: Writing $1-\cos\theta+i\sin\theta=2\sin\frac{\theta}{2}\,i\,e^{-i\theta/2}$ and taking the reciprocal, the real part simplifies to $\dfrac{1}{2}$.

questions.q: $\displaystyle\int_{0}^{\pi/2}\dfrac{\sin^{1000}x\,dx}{\sin^{1000}x+\cos^{1000}x}$ is equal to
questions.explanation: By the property $\int_0^a f(x)dx=\int_0^a f(a-x)dx$, this integral equals its complementary cosine version, so each equals half of $\pi/2$, i.e. $\pi/4$.

questions.q: If $1 + \sin\theta + \sin^2\theta + \ldots$ upto $\infty = 2\sqrt{3} + 4$, then $\theta =$
questions.explanation: Sum of infinite GP: $\dfrac{1}{1-\sin\theta}=2\sqrt3+4 \Rightarrow \sin\theta=\dfrac{\sqrt3}{2} \Rightarrow \theta=\pi/3$.

questions.q: $\displaystyle\lim_{x\to0}\dfrac{xe^x-\sin x}{x}$ is equal to
questions.explanation: Splitting the limit: $\lim(e^x) - \lim\dfrac{\sin x}{x} = 1-1=0$.

questions.q: If $\tan^{-1}(x^2+y^2) = \alpha$ then $\dfrac{dy}{dx}$ is equal to
questions.explanation: Since $\alpha$ is constant, $x^2+y^2=\tan\alpha$ is constant; differentiating gives $2x+2yy'=0$, so $y'=-x/y$.

questions.q: The simplified form of $i^n + i^{n+1} + i^{n+2} + i^{n+3}$ is
The two curves $x^3 - 3xy^2 + 2 = 0$ and $3x^2y - y^3 = 2$
options: Cut each other at right angle
questions.explanation: Differentiating both curves gives slopes $m_1=\dfrac{x^2-y^2}{2xy}$ and $m_2=\dfrac{-2xy}{x^2-y^2}$; since $m_1m_2=-1$ always, the curves are orthogonal (cut at right angle).

questions.q: The equation of the normal to the curve $y(1+x^2) = 2 - x$ where the tangent crosses x-axis is
questions.explanation: Where the curve meets the x-axis, $y=0 \Rightarrow x=2$; differentiating gives slope $-1/5$ at (2,0), so the normal slope is 5, giving $y=5(x-2)$, i.e. $5x-y-10=0$.

questions.q: The maximum value of $\left(\dfrac{1}{x}\right)^x$ is
questions.explanation: Let $y=x^{-x}$; taking logs and differentiating, the maximum occurs at $x=1/e$, giving $y=e^{1/e}$.

questions.q: The solution for the differential equation $\dfrac{dy}{y} + \dfrac{dx}{x} = 0$ is
questions.explanation: Integrating, $\ln y+\ln x=c_1 \Rightarrow \ln(xy)=c_1 \Rightarrow xy=c$.

questions.q: The order and degree of the differential equation $\left[1+\left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)^2+\sin\left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)\right]^{3/4} = \dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}$
questions.explanation: The highest derivative is $d^2y/dx^2$, so order is 2; since the equation contains $\sin(dy/dx)$, a transcendental function of a derivative, the degree is not defined.

questions.q: If $\vec{a}$ and $\vec{b}$ are unit vectors then what is the angle between $\vec{a}$ and $\vec{b}$ for $\sqrt{3}\vec{a}-\vec{b}$ to be unit vector?
questions.explanation: $|\sqrt3\vec a-\vec b|^2=1 \Rightarrow 3-2\sqrt3\cos\theta+1=1 \Rightarrow \cos\theta=\dfrac{\sqrt3}{2} \Rightarrow \theta=30°$.

questions.q: The sum of $1^{st}$ n terms of the series $\dfrac{1^2}{1}+\dfrac{1^2+2^2}{1+2}+\dfrac{1^2+2^2+3^2}{1+2+3}+\ldots$
questions.explanation: The $k$-th term is $\dfrac{k(k+1)(2k+1)/6}{k(k+1)/2}=\dfrac{2k+1}{3}$; summing this from $k=1$ to $n$ gives $\dfrac{n(n+2)}{3}$.

questions.q: The $11^{th}$ term in the expansion of $\left(x+\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{x}}\right)^{14}$ is
Suppose $\vec{a}+\vec{b}+\vec{c}=0$, $|\vec{a}|=3$, $|\vec{b}|=5$, $|\vec{c}|=7$, then the angle between $\vec{a}$ & $\vec{b}$ is
questions.explanation: Since $\vec c=-(\vec a+\vec b)$, $49=9+25+2\vec a\cdot\vec b \Rightarrow \vec a\cdot\vec b=7.5$; $\cos\theta=7.5/15=0.5 \Rightarrow \theta=\pi/3$.

questions.q: If $a=3, b=4, c=5$ each one of $\vec a,\vec b$ & $\vec c$ is perpendicular to the sum of the remaining then $|\vec a+\vec b+\vec c|$ is equal to
questions.explanation: The perpendicularity conditions make $\vec a,\vec b,\vec c$ mutually perpendicular, so $|\vec a+\vec b+\vec c|^2=9+16+25=50$, giving $5\sqrt2$.

questions.q: If the straight lines $2x + 3y - 3 = 0$ and $x + ky + 7 = 0$ are perpendicular, then the value of k is
questions.explanation: Slopes are $-2/3$ and $-1/k$; perpendicularity gives $\left(-\dfrac{2}{3}\right)\left(-\dfrac{1}{k}\right)=-1 \Rightarrow k=-2/3$.

questions.q: The rate of change of area of a circle with respect to its radius at r = 2 cms is
questions.explanation: $A=\pi r^2 \Rightarrow dA/dr=2\pi r$; at $r=2$, $dA/dr=4\pi$.

questions.q: The value of $\tan\dfrac{\pi}{8}$ is equal to
questions.explanation: $\tan(\pi/8)=\sqrt2-1=\dfrac{1}{\sqrt2+1}$ after rationalizing.

questions.q: Area lying between the curves $y^2 = 2x$ and $y = x$ is
questions.explanation: The curves meet at $x=0,2$; Area $=\int_0^2(\sqrt{2x}-x)\,dx=\dfrac{2}{3}$ sq. units.

questions.q: If $P(A\cap B) = 7/10$ and $P(B) = 17/20$, where P stands for probability then $P(A|B)$ is equal to
The coefficient of variation of two distributions are 60 and 70. The standard deviation are 21 and 16 respectively, then their mean is
questions.explanation: Mean $=\dfrac{SD}{CV}\times100$ gives $\dfrac{21}{60}\times100=35$ for the first distribution and $\dfrac{16}{70}\times100\approx22.85$ for the second; KEA's key accepted options 1, 3 and 4 (as per KEA key).

questions.q: Two cards are drawn at random from a pack of 52 cards. The probability of these two being "Aces" is
If $\sin^{-1}x + \sin^{-1}y = \dfrac{\pi}{2}$, then $x^2$ is equal to
questions.explanation: Since $\sin^{-1}y=\dfrac{\pi}{2}-\sin^{-1}x=\cos^{-1}x$, we get $y=\sqrt{1-x^2}$, so $x^2=1-y^2$.

questions.q: The value of $\displaystyle\int_{2}^{8}\dfrac{\sqrt{10-x}}{\sqrt{x}+\sqrt{10-x}}\,dx$ is
questions.explanation: Using $\int_a^bf(x)dx=\int_a^bf(a+b-x)dx$ with $a+b=10$, adding the integral to itself with $x\to10-x$ gives $2I=\int_2^8 1\,dx=6$, so $I=3$.

questions.q: The contrapositive of the converse of the statement "If x is a prime number then x is odd" is
options: If x is not a prime number then x is odd.
If x is not an odd number then x is not a prime number.
If x is a prime number then it is not odd.
If x is not a prime number then x is not an odd.
questions.explanation: Converse: "If x is odd then x is prime." Its contrapositive: "If x is not prime then x is not odd."

questions.q: Two dice are thrown simultaneously, the probability of obtaining a total score of 5 is
questions.explanation: Favourable outcomes for sum 5: (1,4),(2,3),(3,2),(4,1) = 4 out of 36, giving $1/9$.

questions.q: If $A=\begin{bmatrix}\cos2\theta & -\sin2\theta\\ \sin2\theta & \cos2\theta\end{bmatrix}$ and $A + A^T = I$, where I is the unit matrix of $2\times2$ & $A^T$ is the transpose of A, then the value of $\theta$ is equal to
questions.explanation: $A+A^T=\begin{bmatrix}2\cos2\theta&0\\0&2\cos2\theta\end{bmatrix}=I \Rightarrow \cos2\theta=\dfrac12 \Rightarrow \theta=\pi/6$.

questions.q: If $A=\begin{bmatrix}3 & 1\\ -1 & 2\end{bmatrix}$ then $A^2 - 5A$ is equal to
questions.explanation: $A^2=\begin{bmatrix}8&5\\-5&3\end{bmatrix}$ and $5A=\begin{bmatrix}15&5\\-5&10\end{bmatrix}$, so $A^2-5A=\begin{bmatrix}-7&0\\0&-7\end{bmatrix}=-7I$.

questions.q: The value of x if $x(\hat{i}+\hat{j}+\hat{k})$ is a unit vector is
questions.explanation: $|x|\sqrt{1+1+1}=1 \Rightarrow x=\pm\dfrac{1}{\sqrt3}$.

questions.q: If $x = 2 + 3\cos\theta$ and $y = 1 - 3\sin\theta$ represent a circle then the centre and radius is
questions.explanation: $(x-2)^2+(y-1)^2=9(\cos^2\theta+\sin^2\theta)=9$, so centre (2,1) and radius 3.

questions.q: The vector equation of the plane which is at a distance of $\dfrac{3}{\sqrt{14}}$ from the origin and the normal from the origin is $2\hat{i}-3\hat{j}+\hat{k}$ is
questions.explanation: The unit normal is $\dfrac{2\hat i-3\hat j+\hat k}{\sqrt{14}}$, so the plane equation $\vec r\cdot\hat n=d$ becomes $\vec r\cdot(2\hat i-3\hat j+\hat k)=3$.

questions.q: Find the co-ordinates of the foot of the perpendicular drawn from the origin to the plane $5y + 8 = 0$:
questions.explanation: The plane $y=-8/5$ is parallel to the xz-plane, so the foot of the perpendicular from the origin is $(0,-8/5,0)$.

questions.q: If $\cos\alpha, \cos\beta, \cos\gamma$ are the direction cosines of a vector $\vec a$, then $\cos2\alpha + \cos2\beta + \cos2\gamma$ is equal to
questions.explanation: $\cos^2\alpha+\cos^2\beta+\cos^2\gamma=1$, so $\sum(2\cos^2-1)=2(1)-3=-1$.

questions.q: The value of $\sin1° + \sin2° + \ldots + \sin359°$ is equal to
questions.explanation: Terms pair up as $\sin k°+\sin(360-k)°=0$ for $k=1..179$, plus $\sin180°=0$, giving a total of 0.

questions.q: Integrating factor of $x\dfrac{dy}{dx} - y = x^4 - 3x$ is
questions.explanation: Dividing by x gives $\dfrac{dy}{dx}-\dfrac{y}{x}=x^3-3$, a linear equation with $P=-1/x$; IF $=e^{\int -1/x\,dx}=e^{-\ln x}=1/x$.
